talk_track: Charles - I ran platform engineering at Ripple and PayPal, where the work was turning architecture standards into a developer platform people actually shipped on: deploy cycles went from hours to minutes, and at PayPal that platform served 9,000+ developers. Your Lead Platform Engineer posting asks the hire to 'design and implement automation and self-service workflows using infrastructure-as-code, APIs, and developer platforms to reduce developer friction,' working alongside a Cloud Architect who already owns platform strategy and standards. Read plainly, that is a strategy-to-delivery gap rather than a headcount gap - the standards are written, and nobody has the capacity to make them the default path engineers take. Built In shows the two versions of that role reposted at 15 and 22 days, which is what usually happens when you are hiring for the translation layer between architecture and delivery; that market is thin. Meanwhile the same JD asks the hire to champion AI-assisted development, which lands on pipelines that have to verify what gets generated - verification capacity, not more implementers, is what makes that safe. What has the platform team not shipped this quarter?
